author: Nima Kamali and Mert Turna

captions.comparison_map: Original architectural comparison. OpenPI predicts a direct action velocity; Scalar-Pi retains its transformer vector output but differentiates an input-dot scalar. The input-dot construction also appears in a U-Net setting in Sun et al.; EnergyFlow instead pools temporal features into a scalar head and uses a negative action gradient as a score. These are different implementations and objectives, not a controlled empirical comparison. The scalar-potential construction itself is not claimed as new.
captions.contrast_intervals: Eight pre-specified descriptive paired contrasts copied exactly from the saved report. Points are percentage-point differences and bars are the original 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 0). The primary P-B1,K10 contrast is highlighted. Intervals are not adjusted for multiplicity and do not resolve the study's hardware-eligibility limitation.
captions.future_studies: Proposed studies only: training-time trajectory supervision, event/waypoint conditioning, invariant-potential geometry, future-feature prediction, and a discrete-gripper/convex-noise generator. None is evaluated in this report. Every proposal requires matched direct/scalar controls and task-success evaluation; smoothness, safety and distributional coverage require their own measured endpoints.
captions.literature_evidence: Within-paper results reported by other studies, redrawn from their numerical reports. Each panel uses its own task/data/model protocol; gains are not pooled and the panels are not a cross-paper leaderboard. There is no Scalar-Pi bar. These results motivate controlled follow-up experiments rather than predict the effect of adding a component here.
captions.study_design: Factorial protocol: three trained arms at three seeds, one released reference, two Euler-step counts, four suites of ten tasks, and fifty initial states per task. Nine trained checkpoints contribute 36,000 episodes and the single released checkpoint contributes 4,000. B1 and P share reset output initialization; B0 retains the pretrained output. Hardware eligibility remains unresolved.
captions.success_overview: Observed success by suite and solver steps. For trained arms, shapes mark seeds 17, 42, 93 and short horizontal bars show their mean; the released reference has one checkpoint and therefore one point, not three seeds. Overall rates weight the four equally sized suites equally. No confidence intervals are constructed from these seed points.
captions.task_differences: Exploratory task heterogeneity on the ten long-horizon tasks. Heatmap cells show trained-seed mean P minus B1 or the single released reference, in percentage points. The two selected K10 tasks reproduce the quoted Moka 53.3% versus 38% and mugs 64% versus 100% rates. Seed-level points expose variation; the horizontal released line is one checkpoint, not a repeated seed. Selection is descriptive and does not support a mechanistic smoothness explanation.
captions.task_heatmap_all: All forty benchmark tasks, with P minus B1 and P minus the released checkpoint at both solver settings. Trained-arm rates are averages over three seeds and fifty initial states per seed; reference rates use one checkpoint and fifty initial states. Cells show percentage-point differences, not task-level confidence intervals. Task labels are abbreviated from the public episode descriptions; the complete descriptions and numeric cells are in figure-data.json.

literature_evidence.name: Hermite
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Four-suite LIBERO average; 50 rollouts per task, 40 tasks, 2,000 episodes per method; T10/W5, ten denoising steps, 30,000 training updates.

literature_evidence.name: Faithful Plans
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Custom Block-AR + suffix conditioning versus Custom Block-AR + NGM; 500 episodes per suite; one training run per variant. Not a vanilla pi0.5 baseline.

literature_evidence.name: ESP
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Authors' ten-step flow baseline versus one-step ESP; reported values 89.1 +/- 1.2 and 91.8 +/- 1.4. The wide ESP variant in Table II is a separate configuration, not this plotted comparison.

literature_evidence.name: Drifting
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Full-model updates with a fresh head; pi0.5 97.10 versus drifting 98.32. Frozen-VLM expert-only drifting is a different setting and reports 94.57, not the plotted 98.32.

literature_evidence.name: SAVLA
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Identical ten-percent per-task data; budget-matched reduced GR00T N1.5 baseline; 200 evaluation episodes, three seeds.

literature_evidence.name: AnyCam
literature_evidence.protocol_detail: Unseen agent-camera perturbations, small/medium/large levels, averaged across four suites. pi0.5, view-augmented pi0.5, and AnyCam + frozen pi0.5. Different from standard LIBERO camera evaluation.
